findings.message: The new check covers only one side of the fix: that hooks/hooks.json holds no keys Codex refuses. Nothing in the bash/coreutils suites asserts the other side, that `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` still names `./hooks/mod.json` and that `mod.json` lists `./register.tsx`. If either is dropped, the mod stops loading in Claude Code, and only `run-mod-tests.sh` would notice. That suite needs `bun` and `claude` and may not run in CI. The CLAUDE.md line also says `run-codex-plugin-tests.sh` 'checks it', which reads as covering this wiring. Fix: add an assertion that the Claude manifest's `hooks` names `./hooks/mod.json` and that `mod.json`'s `modules` contains `./register.tsx`, or narrow the CLAUDE.md wording.

The key check runs `set(json.load(...))` without first checking that the top level is a JSON object. A top-level array of strings such as `["description"]` or `[]` yields only allowed or empty 'keys', so the check passes even though Codex would reject the file. A non-object top level should fail. Fix: assert `isinstance(d, dict)` and print a marker such as `not-an-object` when it is not.
